spine.last_session: Ran Wave 0 to completion across seven experiments plus three follow-up probes. Layer 0 was refuted then rescued by one key; D6's mechanism was replaced with a per-worktree form; Step 3 was inverted. Dispatched the SPEC amendment. Nothing implemented.

open_risks.text: Layer 0 is refuted — the sandbox blocks loopback and no allowlist can reach it, while on defaults a denied command is silently re-run unsandboxed and reported as succeeded, so containment is illusory exactly where it matters

A broad Bash(*) allow is silently discarded in auto mode and the command falls through to the classifier — Step 3 as written yields strictly less autonomy than enumerated narrow prefixes, and the rejection is visible only at debug level

The temp-index checkpoint captures nested repos as empty gitlinks — the eight worktrees holding agent work are captured not at all, and plain add -A silently drops tracked-but-ignored files so --force is a correctness requirement

Rollback undoes itself — converge promotes whenever live differs from local main, so a rolled-back release is re-promoted at the next session start or stop unless a human also moves the main pointer back

A PR that omits the hooks key strips every hook from live and passes validation — repo-owned absence means deletion, converge itself is removed, and permissions.deny has the identical shape, which Step 1 edits directly

Unclassified settings keys land once then freeze — sandbox, defaultMode and permissions.ask ship on first introduction, after which live wins permanently and every later repo revision is silently inert

key_decisions.title: D2 guards the live installed copy, not version-controlled source
The D6 checkpoint runs at the worktree root and requires --force
Allow rules enumerate narrow prefixes; a broad Bash star rule is counterproductive
Layer 0 survives on one key; the default sandbox configuration is unsafe
Oversight-reducing changes wait for direct user confirmation
